title: Solstice Bio - SOC2/ISO27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood and Solstice Bio reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, discussed access to reports, controls mapping for PHI workflows, RBAC/SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM), audit log retention and delivery, KMS/encryption options, and data residency. Action items: share SOC2 report and ISO certificate, provide controls mapping doc, confirm log export options and retention, and schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for log ingestion to customer SIEM.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (CISO, Solstice Bio), Marcus Lee (Head of IT), Sana Ahmad (Compliance), Tom Walker (VP Product)

Auto-summary: Quick SOC 2 / ISO posture review. Customer asked for reports access, controls mapping and details on RBAC/SSO and audit logs. SE covered KMS options and log export patterns. Agreed on follow-ups and sharing artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jamie from Redwood, with me is Rafael our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:06] Priya: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in, we've been asked to do a security posture review ahead of procurement.
[00:12] Jamie: Totally, that's exactly what this call is for. We'll walk through our SOC2 and ISO posture, what artifacts we can share, and then Rafael can dig into the technical bits like audit logs, KMS and SSO.
[00:21] Marcus: Great, our main asks up front: 1) We need a copy of SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs or access to a trust center, 2) controls mapping so our audit team can map Redwood controls to our internal controls, 3) how logs/PII are handled and can be shipped to our SIEM, and 4) KMS options for customer-managed keys.
[00:40] Rafael: Perfect. Quick note, for SOC2 we have a standard Type II report we can provide under NDA, and for ISO 27001 we have a certificate plus statement of applicability. We also have a Trust Center portal where customers can request read-only access to certain artifacts.
[00:53] Priya: On the trust center, is that self-service or do you provision access per request? We have different teams that want different visibility.
[00:59] Jamie: It's per-customer, you request access and we grant role-based visibility. Typically we provision a compliance viewer role. It supports SSO via SAML so you can use your IdP.
[01:10] Priya: Good. Is SCIM supported for group sync?
[01:13] Rafael: Yes, SCIM is supported for provisioning groups and syncing membership which we recommend if you want automated RBAC. There are a couple of caveats around nested groups that we can show in the controls mapping doc.
[01:24] Tom: Can we get a quick summary on audit logs — what is captured and retention?
[01:28] Rafael: Sure. We capture admin actions, API requests (including token, route, model used), access events, and configuration changes. Default retention in hosted mode is 90 days in the UI, but we can export logs to S3 or push to a syslog/HTTPS endpoint for longer retention. Some customers ship to Splunk or Datadog.
[01:45] Marcus: If we push to our S3, can we keep them in our own bucket?
[01:48] Rafael: Yes, we support customer-managed S3 buckets with cross-account access. We also support streaming via Kinesis and direct HTTPS ingestion. For on-prem/private deployments obviously logs stay in your environment.
[01:58] Priya: And what about PII — are logs redacted by default?
[02:01] Rafael: We redact high sensitivity fields by default in system logs; request/response bodies are not stored long-term unless you enable debug logging or request retention features. For PHI workflows we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict retention and encryption.
[02:15] Jamie: Also note we offer encryption at rest by default. For customer-managed keys we interoperate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault, with support for key rotation and HSM-backed keys for on-prem variants.
[02:26] Sana: Do you provide a KMS integration that allows us to bring our own key (BYOK) so Redwood never sees plaintext keys?
[02:31] Rafael: Yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private customers. For hosted, we offer a bring-your-key option backed by KMS where the key policy ensures Redwood has limited decrypt rights — we can send the exact architecture diagram in the controls mapping doc.
[02:46] Priya: For the SOC 2 report, what's typically redacted? We need to give it to our audit vendor.
[02:51] Jamie: We can provide a redacted Type II report and sign an NDA; sensitive customer names and internal IPs are usually redacted. Some customers request a bridge letter if the report is slightly older.
[02:59] Priya: Okay please send that. Also we need a crosswalk between SOC 2 controls and ISO 27001 clauses — can you do that?
[03:05] Rafael: Yep, Rafael: we have an internal controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our SOC 2 sections to ISO 27001 controls and to typical customer control IDs. I'll share that, it's the doc most auditors want.
[03:16] Marcus: On data residency — we operate in EU for PHI. Does Redwood guarantee region locking?
[03:21] Jamie: We offer region-specific hosting in EU and US. For Private deployments you can choose on-prem. For Dedicated we can ensure data and compute stay in the selected region with contractual terms. We'll add the specific region SLA language to the DPA.
[03:36] Tom: Any third-party pen tests or vuln scans we should know about?
[03:40] Rafael: We run quarterly internal scanning and annual external penetration tests; summary results are in the trust center. We can provide redacted pentest reports under an NDA.
[03:50] Priya: Regarding personnel controls, who has production access?
[03:53] Jamie: Production access is strictly limited; we use RBAC, just-in-time access for privileged ops, with audit trails. We'll include an access matrix in the controls mapping doc.
[04:04] Marcus: If we need logs forwarded to our SIEM in real time, what's the latency?
[04:09] Rafael: Typically sub-second to a few seconds for streaming pipelines, dependent on network. For S3 exports it's batched every few minutes. We can do a short benchmark if required.
[04:19] Priya: One of our compliance folks asked about preservation for legal holds — can logs be preserved beyond normal retention?
[04:24] Rafael: Yes, we can place retention overrides or export them to your archive bucket for indefinite holds. That's part of the Dedicated/Private feature set.
[04:33] Sana: About the trust center access, you said SSO is supported. Does it support SCIM role provisioning for read-only compliance users?
[04:40] Rafael: Yes, we typically create a "Compliance Viewer" role and provision via SCIM groups. We'll outline the exact SCIM attributes.
[04:47] Jamie: Quick pause, does anyone have additional must-haves we didn't call out?
[04:52] Tom: We want to ensure key rotation practices are documented and that Redwood's KMS usage meets our vendor risk checklist.
[04:58] Priya: Also need to confirm data separation if multi-tenant.
[05:01] Rafael: For multi-tenant hosted we isolate tenants at the data plane level using encryption and logical separation; Dedicated gives you tenant isolation via dedicated pools. We'll include diagrams.
[05:12] Jamie: Next steps I'm hearing: we'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO cert under NDA, Rafael to send controls mapping + architecture notes for KMS and logging, Marcus to give SIEM endpoint and retention needs, and we'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive.
[05:25] Priya: That works. Can we tentatively lock the deep dive for next week?
[05:28] Jamie: Sure how about 10/6?
[05:30] Marcus: Works for me.
[05:31] Sana: Works.
[05:32] Jamie: Great, I'll send calendar invite and the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[05:36] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Caveats / Notes: Transcription has some mis-hearings around model names and internal product terms; omitted low-level kernel/latency details since this was compliance focused. Artifacts referenced: SOC2 Type II report (redacted), ISO 27001 certificate, controls mapping spreadsheet, trust center access request form, DPA and legal redlines.

End of transcript.
